subject: Residency guarantees for private VPC storage — snapshot & deletion workflow

Laura —

Thanks for taking this. We're close to signing but have a few outstanding questions around the private VPC option and how Redwood handles customer-controlled storage and deletions. I attached a short spreadsheet with numbered items (Veridian_DataResidency_Qs.xlsx) to make it easier. High level asks:

- If we choose customer-managed storage (S3 in our account), does Redwood ever hold a secondary copy of our data outside the VPC or in the control plane?
- How are snapshots and backups handled? Are snapshots taken in our account or by Redwood? If Redwood manages snapshots, can you provide the retention/deletion process?
- We need an auditable proof-of-delete artifact we can provide to our auditors. What format and timeline can Redwood provide?
- Is there a customer-triggerable API to immediately tombstone/remove tenant data, and what are recovery windows?

We'd appreciate a clear, concise explanation we can share with our security & procurement teams.

Thanks,
Chris Walsh

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Residency guarantees for private VPC storage — technical details

Chris / Laura —

Below is a concise technical summary addressing each of the numbered items in your spreadsheet. I kept timings conservative so you can present realistic SLAs to your auditors.

1) Secondary copies / control plane
- For Redwood Private (VPC deployment) the inference runtime mounts storage that lives in your cloud account (S3 buckets or EBS volumes) using the IAM roles/permissions you provide. By default Redwood does not copy tenant user data out of your account. The reductive exception: optional control-plane metadata (route, model version, request logs) may be buffered in a customer-configurable control-plane store; customers can elect zero retention for control-plane logs.

2) Snapshots and backups
- Two modes: Customer-managed snapshots (default recommended) and Redwood-managed archival snapshots (opt-in).
  - Customer-managed: snapshots are created as snapshots in your account (EBS/S3 object versions) under your billing and lifecycle. Uptake: automated snapshot orchestration runs in your account on a schedule you choose (daily/weekly). Deletion is governed by your lifecycle policies.
  - Redwood-managed archival snapshots: if enabled, Redwood creates encrypted archives in a Redwood-managed bucket. These are encrypted with a Redwood key distinct from your KMS; we provide an export and proof-of-delete when asked. Note: this mode gives convenience but means Redwood retains an encrypted copy until deletion is processed.

3) Deletion/tombstone process and recovery windows
- Tenant tombstone flow (customer-triggerable API or Console):
  - Step A: Tombstone marker placed on tenant (instant). System stops accepting new writes and invalidates caches (0–60s).
  - Step B: Asynchronous purge of ephemeral caches and KV caches (minutes).
  - Step C: Snapshot lifecycle: if customer-managed, we hand off guidance and optionally a script to remove snapshots/versions; if Redwood-managed, we schedule archive deletion and run a zeroization sequence.
  - Recovery window: configurable between 0 and 14 days. Default safe window is 7 days to allow emergency undeletion. After recovery window expires, objects are zeroed and KMS keys are scheduled for rotation/destruction per your KMS policy.

4) Proof-of-delete artifact
- What we can deliver: a signed bundle containing
  - list_of_deleted_objects.csv (S3 object keys and checksums)
  - deletion_manifest.json (timestamps, sequence ids)
  - signed_audit_statement.pdf (signed by Redwood operations, includes software version + deletion run id)
  - Cloud provider snapshot IDs (if applicable) + deletion confirmations from the cloud provider console exports
- Delivery timeline: if Redwood-managed archival snapshots were used, proof-of-delete can be produced within 48–72 hours of the deletion job completing. If customer-managed snapshots, we provide the manifest and an ops playbook and can validate via a mutually-agreed scan (time depends on customer schedule).

5) KMS / key material
- If you use customer-managed KMS keys for storage encryption, destroying the key renders data irrecoverable; we recommend an explicit key destruction confirmation step in the proof bundle. If Redwood-managed keys were used we include key-rotation logs and a signed attestation of zeroization steps.

6) Audit logs and evidence
- Console: per-tenant audit export (CSV) with timestamps for tombstone, deletion job start/completion, and operator IDs.
- We can produce a time-stamped, signed tarball (proof_of_delete_bundle.tar.gz) containing the files above; this artifact is suitable for SOC2 reviewers.

Attachments: I attached a short diagram that shows the snapshot handoff and deletion flow: redwood_snapshot_flow.pdf.

If you want, we can also provide a short runbook that your ops team can execute to cutover to customer-managed snapshots and a sample script to call the tenant-tombstone API.

–Karthik

Karthik —

This is helpful, thanks. Two follow-ups quickly:

- For the Recovery window: is the 0–14 day window enforced by Redwood code (i.e., immutable once set), or can an operator override to do a forced immediate purge? We need the ability to force immediate destruction under certain legal directives.
- For the signed bundle: will the bundle include direct cloud-provider deletion confirmations (exported API responses) or just Redwood attestations? Auditors prefer provider confirmations when customer-managed snapshots were removed.

If you can confirm those two points I think we can proceed. Also Tue 5/5 at 10am PT works for a walkthrough — I'll invite our security architect.

Chris

Chris —

Quick confirmations and next steps:

- Forced immediate purge: yes. For customers with a legal directive we support a forced purge workflow. That action requires a joint-auth flow (customer operator + Redwood ops) and is auditable in the console. The forced purge bypasses the configured recovery window and triggers immediate zeroization; we log all operator IDs and produce an auditable event stream. We treat forced purges as an emergency operation and require sign-off before execution.

- Proof bundle contents: when snapshots are customer-managed we include the cloud-provider deletion exports in the bundle (API response logs and snapshot IDs) where available. For Redwood-managed archives we provide the signed_audit_statement and provider confirmations for any provider-side operations we invoked.

Next steps:
- I'll generate a sample proof_of_delete_bundle.tar.gz (includes list_of_deleted_objects.csv + signed_audit_statement.pdf + provider_export.txt) and upload it to the shared drive. You can find it here: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/VER-2026-021/residency-evidence (internal link above).
- Marissa will send a short runbook and the tenant-tombstone API sample call for your infra team to test.
- Meeting confirmed Tue 5/5 10am PT — calendar invite to follow.

If you need the joint-auth flow to be automated via a DocuSign approval step we can add that as a one-off integration (we've done this for two enterprise customers).

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Laura Bennett
